```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set( collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>" )
has_fixest <- requireNamespace( "fixest", quietly = TRUE )
```

A study of nonprofit mergers with **npmerger** has three stages. Each one
is a single function, and each writes its tables to one project database.

| Stage | Function | What it builds | Reads |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Mergers | `build_merger_data()` | Schedule N labels, merger cases, donor and recipient tables, Part VII rosters, leadership outcomes, typology | Schedule N, plus the returns of the organizations involved |
| 2. Matching | `build_match_data()` | The full 990 panel, the research sample, the comparison pool, candidates, balance | Every 990 and 990-EZ return |
| 3. Model data | `build_model_data()` | Treated units, control sets, donor sums, the outcome panel | Stages 1 and 2 |

The models then run from the stage 3 data: `merger_did()` for the main
estimates, `did_breakouts()`, `did_sensitivity()`, and
`did_event_study()`.

**Stage 1 stands on its own.** Finding mergers needs only Schedule N and
the returns of the organizations that filed it or received assets. If you
only want a list of mergers, stop there. Stages 2 and 3 are for comparing
merger recipients with organizations that did not merge.

```{r}
library( npmerger )
library( data.table )
```

## The project folder

`merger_project()` creates a folder that holds one build:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
proj <- merger_project( "~/Documents/NPMERGER" )
```

```
NPMERGER/
  PANEL990/          panel990 download cache (reused by later builds)
  npmerger.duckdb    every table, plus build_log and build_settings
  logs/              one log per stage run, <stage>-<time>.log
  results/           model estimates
  README.md          tables, row counts, and the build log
```

`build_merger_database()` runs the stages into that folder:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
build_merger_database(
  project = proj,
  stages  = c( "merger", "match", "model" ),
  years   = efile_years()
)
```

A fresh build of every e-file year (2009-2025), run in November 2026:

| Stage | Time | Main tables |
|---|---|---|
| merger | 54 min on a first run (including the downloads), 42 min once cached | 63,706 Schedule N filings; 12,684 merger cases; 1.4 million Part VII person-years |
| match | 7 min | 6.2 million organization-years; 3.0 million in the pool; 4,507 treated recipients |
| model | under 1 min | 4,507 units; about 75,000 candidate rows per specification; 629,000 organization-years |

The download cache is 8 GB and the database 1.6 GB. Running every model in
the paper from the model stage takes under a minute.

Each stage reads what it needs from the database, so you can rerun a later
stage, for example with different matching calipers, without repeating
the earlier ones:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
build_merger_database(
  project    = proj,
  stages     = c( "match", "model" ),
  match_args = list( ntee_chars = 3L )
)
```

Every stage run writes a log with the package versions, git commit,
settings, a timestamped line for each step, and `sessionInfo()`. It also
adds a row to the `build_log` table.

## Stage 1: find the mergers

`build_merger_data()` downloads Schedule N, classifies every filing, and
builds the tables about each merger. Here it runs offline on the bundled
extract of 2021 filings:

```{r}
ex <- npmerger_example()

md <-
  build_merger_data(
    sn       = ex$sn,
    evidence = ex$evidence,
    core     = ex$core,
    names    = ex$names,
    bmf_data = ex$bmf,
    ratios   = FALSE,
    verbose  = FALSE
  )

md
```

On the full data, the same call takes `years` and a cache folder instead
of the pre-fetched tables:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
md <-
  build_merger_data(
    years = efile_years(),
    path  = proj$cache
  )
```

Two of the tables describe the merger itself rather than the filings:

```{r}
md$typology[ , .( MERGER_ID, TYPE, TYPOLOGY, RATIO ) ] |> head()
```

`md$leadership` records what happened to the two chief executives and the
two boards (`merger_leadership()`). It needs rosters on both sides of the
merger, so it is empty for this one-year extract.

## Stage 2: build the comparison data

`build_match_data()` reads every 990 filer into one panel and finds
comparison organizations for each merger recipient. See
`vignette("matching")` for the design. The rest of this page uses a
simulated panel of 600 organizations, 30 of which absorb another
organization in 2015 and grow by about 30% afterwards.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# simulated panel and merger cases (same as the package tests)
set.seed(1)
n <- 600L
orgs <- data.table(
  EIN2  = sprintf( "ORG-%03d", seq_len(n) ),
  NTEE  = sample( c("E21", "E22", "P20", "B82"), n, TRUE ),
  SIZE  = exp( rnorm(n, 14, 1.2) ),
  FIRST = sample( 2009:2012, n, TRUE ) )
panel <- orgs[ , .( TAX_YEAR = FIRST:(FIRST + 8L) ), by = .( EIN2, NTEE, SIZE ) ]
rec   <- orgs$EIN2[ 1:30 ]
grow  <- with( panel, ifelse( EIN2 %in% rec & TAX_YEAR >= 2015L, 1.3, 1 ) )
panel[ , `:=`(
  OBJECTID = paste0( EIN2, "-", TAX_YEAR ), EZ = FALSE,
  REVENUE  = grow * SIZE * exp( rnorm(.N, 0, 0.1) ),
  ASSETS   = grow * 1.5 * SIZE * exp( rnorm(.N, 0, 0.1) ),
  EMPLOYEES = round( SIZE / 8e4 ), NTEE_SOURCE = "bmf", SUBSECTION = "3" ) ]
panel[ , `:=`(
  EXPENSES = REVENUE * runif(.N, 0.9, 1.05), LIABILITIES = ASSETS * runif(.N, 0.1, 0.6),
  CASH = ASSETS * runif(.N, 0.05, 0.3), STAFF_EXP = REVENUE * 0.5,
  CONTRIBUTIONS = REVENUE * 0.6, PROGRAM_REVENUE = REVENUE * 0.3,
  INVEST_INCOME = REVENUE * 0.05, OTHER_REVENUE = REVENUE * 0.05 ) ]
panel[ , `:=`(
  SURPLUS = REVENUE - EXPENSES, NET_ASSETS = ASSETS - LIABILITIES,
  FUNC_EXP = EXPENSES, MGMT_EXP = EXPENSES * 0.12,
  REAL_REVENUE = REVENUE, REAL_EXPENSES = EXPENSES, REAL_ASSETS = ASSETS ) ]
panel[ , `:=`(
  MARGIN = SURPLUS / REVENUE, EQUITY_RATIO = NET_ASSETS / ASSETS,
  MONTHS_CASH = CASH / (EXPENSES / 12), NTEE2 = ntee_level(NTEE, 2L) ) ]
setkey( panel, EIN2, TAX_YEAR )

ids <- paste0( "M", 1:30 )
sim <- list(
  cases = data.table(
    MERGER_ID = ids, MERGER_GROUP_ID = ids, TYPE = "merger2", BASIS = "leader",
    AFFILIATED = rep( c(FALSE, TRUE), 15 ),
    DONOR_EIN2 = orgs$EIN2[ 31:60 ], RECIP_EIN2 = rec,
    MERGER_YEAR = 2015L, RECIP_MERGER_YEAR = 2015L ),
  sched_n   = data.table( EIN2 = orgs$EIN2[ 31:60 ], TAX_YEAR = 2015L ),
  transfers = data.table( MERGER_ID = ids, FMV_ASSETS = 1e5, FLAG_OUTLIER = FALSE ),
  typology  = data.table( MERGER_ID = ids, TYPOLOGY = rep( c(
    "Merger of near-equals", "Absorption of a stable smaller organization"), 15 ) ),
  leadership = data.table( MERGER_ID = ids, CEO_CAT = "recipient_ceo_only",
    BOARD_CAT = rep( c("combine_minor", "combine_major"), 15 ) ) )
```

```{r}
mm <-
  build_match_data(
    merger_data = sim,
    panel       = panel,
    verbose     = FALSE
  )

mm
```

On the full data, leave out `panel` and give the cache folder. The panel
is built from the same files stage 1 downloaded:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
mm <- build_match_data( md, path = proj$cache )
```

## Stage 3: assemble the model data

`build_model_data()` does the slow joins once. It keeps one row per
treated recipient with its breakout variables, the closest candidate
controls for every matching specification (plus a match on the combined
recipient and donor baseline), donor sums for the pro forma outcomes, and
only the organization-years the models read.

```{r}
dd <- build_model_data( sim, mm, verbose = FALSE )

dd
```

`max_k` and `max_year_gap` set the largest control sets and calendar-year
gaps any later model can ask for (10 and 2 by default).

## Run the models

Every model reads only `dd`. `merger_did()` gives long-difference
estimates, from two years before the merger to two years after, for each
design:

```{r, eval = has_fixest}
fit <-
  merger_did(
    data     = dd,
    outcomes = c( "LOG_REVENUE", "MARGIN" ),
    keep     = NULL
  )

fit[ , .( design, outcome, estimate, se, n_sets ) ] |>
  knitr::kable( digits = 3 )
```

`keep = NULL` uses every treated unit. The default,
`~ OTHER == FALSE`, drops recipients involved in other mergers in the
window.

The three designs are listed by `did_designs()`. The recipient alone
grows by about the simulated 30% (0.26 log points). The pro forma designs
compare the merged organization with the recipient and donor combined
before the merger. In this simulation the donors are about as large as
their recipients, but the recipients grow by only 30%, so the merged
organization ends up smaller than the two were apart and the pro forma
estimates are negative.

### Breakouts

Interact treatment with any unit-level variable from `did_breakout_vars()`:

```{r, eval = has_fixest}
br <-
  did_breakouts(
    data     = dd,
    by       = "AFFILIATED",
    outcomes = "LOG_REVENUE",
    designs  = "naive | recipient match",
    keep     = NULL
  )

br[ , .( spec, term, estimate, se ) ] |>
  knitr::kable( digits = 3 )
```

### Sensitivity

`did_variants()` lists the paper's variants. Each is a set of
`merger_did()` arguments, so adding one is a single line:

```{r, eval = has_fixest}
v <- did_variants()[ c( "base", "k1", "gap2" ) ]

# use every unit in this small example
v <- lapply( v, modifyList, list( keep = ~ TRUE ) )

# one more: three controls per recipient
v$k3 <- modifyList( v$base, list( k = 3L ) )

sens <-
  did_sensitivity(
    data     = dd,
    variants = v,
    outcomes = "LOG_REVENUE",
    designs  = "naive | recipient match"
  )

sens[ , .( variant, estimate, se, n_sets ) ] |>
  knitr::kable( digits = 3 )
```

### Event study

```{r, eval = has_fixest}
es <-
  did_event_study(
    data     = dd,
    outcomes = "LOG_REVENUE",
    designs  = "naive | recipient match",
    keep     = NULL
  )

es[ , .( E, estimate, se ) ] |>
  knitr::kable( digits = 3 )
```

`did_baseline_means()`, `did_funnel()`, and `did_composition()` describe
the same samples: outcome means at `t-2`, the counts from merger cases to
the units and controls used, and the treated units in each breakout
group.

## Coming back to a project

Everything is in the database, so a later session starts from
`load_model_data()` instead of rebuilding:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
proj <- merger_project( "~/Documents/NPMERGER" )

dd  <- load_model_data( proj )
fit <- merger_did( dd )
```

`load_merger_data()` and `load_match_data()` return the stage 1 and stage
2 objects, and `db_read()` reads any single table:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
db_tables( proj )

db_read( proj, "match_balance" )
```
